prompt.context: Our client, NeuroNow, is a mid-market biopharma company with 2 products in the US market. They have developed a new oral medicine to treat multiple sclerosis (MS) which has successfully passed phase 2 of clinical trials. Before deciding on further investments in phase 3 and commercialization, the client is looking to project revenues for the drug in 2021 and would like to know how soon they can break even on their investment from phase 3 trials onwards.
prompt.question: What factors would you consider when deciding whether to proceed with launching the drug?

clarifying_info.a: Total US population is 300 million in 2020.

clarifying_info.q: What is the incidence rate of MS?
clarifying_info.a: It is estimated that 0.1% of Americans will suffer from MS in 2021.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of MS cases are diagnosed and treated?
clarifying_info.a: 80% of cases will be diagnosed; 90% of the diagnosed population will receive treatment.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of NeuroNow therapy?
clarifying_info.a: $1,000 per month for 12 months per patient, so $12,000 per patient per year.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competing oral MS drugs?
clarifying_info.a: The first oral medication was introduced in 2016 and has gained popularity. Two more oral drugs have entered the market since then. Previously, injectable medicines were the standard of care.
Patients undergo gradual degradation of spinal cord and brain cells; symptoms include impaired movement, speaking, and other senses. No full cure exists; treatments manage symptoms.

exhibits.title: MS Treatment Paradigm
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the share of injectable vs. oral treatments among treated MS patients from 2015 through 2025E (estimated). The chart tracks how treatment mix has shifted over time.

exhibits.title: Market Research Study
exhibits.shows: A pie chart of oral MS drug patient share in 2020, plus qualitative quotes from key stakeholders (a leading neurologist, a top private insurer, and a patient).

data.neurologist_quote: Oral drugs have really transformed how I manage my patients... I can't wait for NeuroNow to be launched as its early clinical trials show fewer cases of serious side effects than the leading incumbents.
data.insurer_quote: Oral MS drugs have proven to be an economic boom... With NeuroNow, we expect a greater benefit as fewer patients will be buying additional drugs to manage common side-effects.
data.patient_quote: I am on Oral Drug 1 and it is really helping with my symptoms however the resultant side-effects are getting tougher to manage.

exhibits.title: Estimated Costs
exhibits.shows: A table of cost heads with their schedule and annual or one-time amounts for NeuroNow's phase 3 and commercialization plan.

framework: 1. Market Size: estimate the number of addressable patients x price per patient per year
a. Incidence rate (MS patients in US population)
b. Diagnosis rate and treatment rate (haircuts on total incidence)
c. Treatment share: oral vs. injectable split and NeuroNow's expected share within oral market
d. Price per dose and number of annual doses per patient
e. Market growth rate over the forecast period
2. Profitability: assess whether investment generates adequate return
a. Revenue: price x patients x duration x market share
b. Costs: phase 3 clinical trial, launch costs, salesforce, marketing, manufacturing/distribution
3. Other risks to weigh before proceeding
c. Competitive response from incumbents or new entrants
d. Regulatory changes affecting pricing or approval

questions.prompt: What is the potential number of MS patients that will be treated with oral drugs over the next 5 years (2021-2025)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build the patient funnel: US Population x incidence rate x diagnosis rate x treatment rate to get total treated patients, then apply the oral-drug share from Exhibit 1. A strong candidate identifies each haircut explicitly and uses the exhibit to read off the oral share for each year. They should note the oral market is growing attractively and was accelerated by COVID-19 in 2020. They should recommend a market research study as the next step to estimate NeuroNow's share.

math.setup: Base: 300mn US population x 0.1% incidence = 300,000 MS cases/year. Apply 80% diagnosis rate x 90% treatment rate = 216,000 treated patients/year (assumed constant). Multiply by oral-drug share each year from Exhibit 1.
math.answer: ~896,400 cumulative oral-drug patients over the 5-year window; ~162,000-194,400 per year.

questions.prompt: What is NeuroNow's expected patient share within the oral MS market, and can the client break even within 5 years?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 2 to support the market share assumption. Strong candidate notes qualitative stakeholder sentiment (neurologist and insurer are positive about fewer side effects) and the competitive landscape (three existing oral drugs; Oral Drug 1 has 60% share). Using 40% share assumption is reasonable given the differentiated side-effect profile. They should then build revenue and cost schedule from Exhibit 3 and compute cumulative profit. A strong candidate flags that peak share may take a few years to materialize post-launch.

math.setup: NeuroNow market share assumed at 40% of oral-drug patients each year. Revenue = NeuroNow patients x $12,000/year. Costs from Exhibit 3: 2020 costs = $100mn trial + $70mn salesforce + $130mn marketing = $300mn. 2021 costs = $100mn launch + $70mn salesforce + $130mn marketing + $200mn mfg = $500mn. 2022-2025 costs = $70mn + $130mn + $200mn = $400mn/year.
steps: 2021: 162,000 x 40% = 64,800 patients x $12,000 = $0.78bn revenue (~$0.8bn), costs $0.5bn, profit $0.3bn, cumulative $0bn (breakeven)
2022: 172,800 x 40% = 69,120 patients x $12,000 = $0.83bn (~$0.8bn), costs $0.4bn, profit $0.4bn, cumulative $0.4bn
2023: 183,600 x 40% = 73,440 patients x $12,000 = $0.88bn (~$0.9bn), costs $0.4bn, profit $0.5bn, cumulative $0.9bn
2024: 183,600 x 40% = 73,440 patients, revenue $0.9bn, costs $0.4bn, profit $0.5bn, cumulative $1.4bn
2025: 194,400 x 40% = 77,760 patients x $12,000 = $0.93bn (~$0.9bn), costs $0.4bn, profit $0.5bn, cumulative $1.9bn
math.answer: Breakeven achieved in just over 1 year of launch (end of 2021). Total 5-year profit of $1.9bn at a 44% margin.

questions.prompt: What are some other risks that NeuroNow could face?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate will organize risks into clear buckets. Key risks include: (1) clinical trial failure — probability of phase 3 success must be factored into expected-value calculations; (2) competitor response — a fast-growing oral MS market will attract incumbents to develop new oral products and new entrants, potentially displacing NeuroNow on clinical utility, economic value, or stakeholder ease; (3) regulatory risks — pharma is highly exposed to pricing regulation and approval changes; (4) supply chain — manufacturing and/or distribution issues internally or with partners.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key risks the client could face in launching NeuroNow?

categories.name: Clinical / Scientific
ideas: Phase 3 trial failure or partial failure
Unexpected safety signals or side effects emerging in larger trial population
Lower-than-expected efficacy vs. existing oral drugs

categories.name: Competitive
ideas: Existing injectable competitors develop new oral formulations
New oral entrants offering better efficacy, fewer side effects, or lower price
Oral Drug 1 (market leader at 60% share) aggressive pricing response

categories.name: Commercial / Market Access
ideas: Insurance coverage denial or restrictive formulary placement
Slow physician adoption if marketing investment underperforms

recommendation: NeuroNow should proceed with phase 3 trials and further investment in commercialization.
The client can expect to break even within 1 year of launch (by end of 2021) and generate $1.9bn in cumulative profit (44% margin) over the 5-year window from 2021 to 2025.

They are entering a growing market — oral MS drug share is expanding from 70% in 2020 to a projected 90% by 2025 — with a differentiated product that has better side-effect profile, strong stakeholder support, and clear unmet patient need.
risks: Failure of phase 3 clinical trial, which would require writing off phase 3 investment (~$100mn) and forgoing the projected $1.9bn profit opportunity.
Emergence of new innovative competitors or next-generation oral MS products that erode the assumed 40% market share.
Regulatory pricing changes that compress the $12,000/year price point.
next_steps: Design phase 3 clinical trial with a representative and adequately powered patient population.
Maintain continuous market intelligence on oral MS drug competitors and NeuroNow's positioning.
Begin salesforce recruitment and organizational planning in parallel with the trial.
Develop marketing campaigns and medical affairs messaging ahead of anticipated launch.
